items.content_html:
Value Prop

GitHub Mobile now allows users to start and track Copilot coding agent tasks directly from their mobile devices. This update extends the centralized view of agent tasks experience to mobile, giving developers a seamless and consistent way to manage their Copilot coding agents on the go. By integrating Copilot agent task management into the GitHub Mobile Home view, developers are empowered to initiate, monitor, and interact with coding tasks anytime, anywhere, increasing flexibility and productivity.

Expected Outcome

With this release, developers can expect improved workflow continuity when away from their desktops. The ability to start, monitor, and manage Copilot agent tasks within GitHub Mobile means users can stay informed and take action on critical coding work, even while mobile. This helps teams remain agile, reduces bottlenecks caused by being away from a computer, and ensures that important agent-driven tasks progress efficiently across platforms.
items.title: Start and track Copilot coding agent tasks in GitHub Mobile [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

GitHub Copilot CLI brings the power of coding agent directly to your terminal, enabling developers to work with AI assistance in their native command-line environment. By integrating seamlessly with your GitHub account, Copilot CLI provides terminal-native access to repositories, issues, and pull requests through natural language commands. With agentic capabilities that can plan and execute complex coding tasks—from building features to debugging and refactoring—developers gain an intelligent collaborator that works where they're most productive. MCP-powered extensibility allows teams to customize and extend capabilities with custom servers, while preview-before-execution ensures developers maintain full control over every action.

Expected Outcome

Development teams can expect to accelerate local development workflows by accessing AI-powered coding assistance without leaving their terminal. Copilot CLI reduces context switching by bringing GitHub integration and coding agent capabilities directly into the command line, allowing developers to query repositories, work with issues and pull requests, and execute complex coding tasks using natural language. Teams using Copilot Pro, Pro+, Business, or Enterprise plans can leverage this tool immediately with their existing subscriptions, gaining productivity improvements in everyday tasks like exploring codebases, implementing features, and debugging.
items.title: Copilot CLI [Public Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

The updated home dashboard introduces an agents module that puts the power of AI-driven workflows at users' fingertips. With the new agents module, users can quickly see, track, and launch agent workflows directly from the dashboard, helping them manage tasks more efficiently and stay focused on their work. The dashboard's enhanced design surfaces recent pull requests, issues, and agent activity, turning the home dashboard into a true productivity hub for developers and teams.

Expected Outcome

Customers can expect a more streamlined workflow on GitHub with greater visibility and control over agent-powered development. By bringing agent activity to the forefront, users can discover and leverage new AI capabilities in their daily projects, reducing context switching and increasing productivity. The updated dashboard ensures users are always up-to-date with their most important work, making GitHub an even more central place for software development.
items.title: Add agents module to the home dashboard [Preview]

This integration helps teams stay focused by reducing context switching and supporting faster, more efficient development. By embedding GitHub's AI-powered development tools into Linear's project management platform, teams can solve issues and ship code without leaving their planning environment.

Expected Outcome

With this integration, customers can expect to resolve issues faster and stay in their flow by seamlessly moving from planning to implementation without manual overhead. Teams will benefit from reduced context switching, improved developer productivity, and a streamlined workflow that empowers them to deliver higher quality code with greater speed and consistency.
items.title: Copilot coding agent + Linear Integration [Public Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

GitHub Copilot for Teams brings AI-powered coding assistance into Microsoft Teams, enabling developers and collaborators to generate, review, and implement code directly within their team's conversations. By allowing users to mention GitHub Copilot in Teams channels, this integration removes context switching between chat and development environments. Teams can now collaborate on code, iterate quickly, and keep everyone aligned in a single, familiar workspace.

Expected Outcome

With GitHub Copilot for Teams, organizations can expect more efficient and collaborative software development workflows. Teams can move from discussion to implementation without leaving Teams, reducing friction and manual handoff. This integration accelerates project delivery, improves transparency, and empowers more stakeholders to participate in the coding process, leading to faster, higher-quality outcomes.
items.title: GitHub Copilot for Teams integration [Public Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

GitHub Copilot for Slack empowers developers and their teams to bring AI-powered coding assistance into everyday Slack conversations. By invoking Copilot coding agent directly in Slack using the GitHub app, teams can generate, iterate, and review code collaboratively. This seamless integration helps eliminate context switching, accelerates development, and makes it easier to involve both technical and non-technical stakeholders in the software creation process.

Expected Outcome

With GitHub Copilot for Slack, organizations can expect faster, more collaborative coding workflows. Developers and stakeholders can move from discussion to implementation in a single conversation, reducing friction and manual handoff. The integration enables teams to generate pull requests, handle bug fixes, and iterate on new features directly within Slack, ultimately increasing productivity and keeping everyone aligned.
items.title: GitHub Copilot for Slack integration [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Copilot code review (CCR) brings together AI-powered code analysis and tool calling with trusted open source tools like ESLint and CodeQL. CCR actively gathers project context to deliver precise, actionable feedback tailored to your team's standards and workflow. By combining large language model (LLM) intelligence with deterministic checks, CCR helps you catch critical security and quality issues, reduce noise, and keep your development process efficient. Seamless handoff to the Copilot coding agent reduces manual fixes and accelerates code review cycles, all within your favorite editors.

Expected Outcome

Teams using Copilot code review can expect higher-quality, more secure code with less manual effort. CCR surfaces reliable findings directly in the pull request, explains issues clearly, and enables one-click fixes with Copilot coding agent handoff. This reduces time spent on reviews and rework, so you can ship features faster and focus on higher-value engineering work. CCR adapts to your team's unique workflows and is available in all major editors, meeting developers wherever they work.
items.title: Agentic Copilot code review, powered by Actions [Public Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

GitHub Code Quality expands code scanning to help developers identify and address code quality issues—like maintainability, reliability, performance, complexity, dead and duplicate code, test coverage, accessibility, and correctness—directly in the pull request experience. This feature builds on our strong security foundation, enabling teams to proactively improve their codebase and deliver higher-quality software, all within their existing GitHub workflows. By integrating quality checks and remediation into the development process, GitHub Code Quality helps organizations reduce technical debt, streamline reviews, and compete with leading tools in the market.

Expected Outcome

With GitHub Code Quality, customers can expect to detect and resolve a broader set of issues earlier in the development cycle. By surfacing actionable insights and autofix suggestions directly in pull requests, teams will spend less time on manual code reviews and rework. This results in more maintainable and reliable code, faster shipping cycles, and a simplified path to higher engineering standards—all without leaving GitHub.
items.title: GitHub Code Quality [Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Expected Outcome

All customers (enterprise, organization, and personal accounts) have access to the Analytics page and can:

  • Track which team members are the top consumers of Copilot Premium requests and how quickly users exhausting their monthly quota.
  • View a premium request usage breakdown by product (Spark, Copilot coding agent Copilot premium request) in the UI, API, and Billing usage report.
  • Identify the most popular premium models used.
items.title: Premium requests analytics page

items.content_html:
Value Prop

CodeQL is the static analysis engine that powers GitHub’s code scanning capabilities. In Pull Requests, it can pinpoint potential vulnerabilities and deliver detailed insights alongside automated remediation suggestions through Copilot Autofix. With this update, CodeQL queries and extraction will focus exclusively on newly introduced code rather than rescanning the entire codebase, streamlining the analysis process.

Expected Outcome

Developers receive even faster feedback during Pull Requests, reducing the time needed to identify and fix emerging vulnerabilities. This speed enhancement aims to make a significant reduction in scan duration with a potential small impact on accuracy on the Pull Requests page. This will help accelerate the remediation process, enabling teams to secure their code more efficiently without slowing down for security.
items.title: Improved incremental CodeQL analysis during Pull Requests for Ruby and Java

items.content_html:
Value Prop

GitHub's Copilot Enterprise & Users Usage dashboard/export provides enterprises essential Copilot usage analytics including active user metrics, feature adoption rates, code completion acceptance, and more with the goal to help enterprise leaders understand how, where, and why Copilot is utilized in their development. With both aggregated dashboard views and user-granular exports, Enterprises gain actionable insights to drive strategic decisions for the first time ever.

Expected Outcome

With the Copilot Enterprise & Users Usage dashboard/export, enterprises can expect to make data-driven decisions about their AI development investment, leading to more effective license allocation and improved developer productivity across teams. Leaders will be able to identify adoption patterns, measure the impact of Copilot on their development workflows, and see how GitHub Copilot investment show up in the development cycle through concrete usage metrics and adoption trends.
items.title: Copilot Enterprise & Users Usage Metrics Dashboard/Export [Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Rust is becoming a more popular languages and more enterprises are adopting it as an alternative to C/C++. Rust support for CodeQL allows organizations to analyse their proprietary Rust codebases for potential security vulnerabilities.

Expected Outcome

Users using Rust to build their applications will start seeing files written in Rust included in the list of files scanned by CodeQL. This means that they will potentially see new CodeQL relevant to Rust. This will help find and fix issues from additional code bases and improve the overall security posture of the applications scanned with CodeQL.
items.title: CodeQL supports Rust [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

C/C++ project are notorious for being tricky to analyse with CodeQL. The main reason is because the tool requires a successful build in order to extract information that is needed for a scan. We are now planning to take an approach similar to Java / C# where you can analyse C/C++ code without relying on 3rd party tools to run a full build. Instead, you can use CodeQL to extract as much of the information as possible, add tolerance to errors, and continue with scans even if not all the code is extracted.

Expected Outcome

With the ability to scan C/C++ without working builds, users will be able to quickly scale CodeQL across their C/C++ repositories. As no build is required, CodeQL and default setup will roll out across your organizations without additional input needed.
items.title: CodeQL can scan C/C++ without a working build [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

GitHub's open-source Accessibility Annotation Toolkit addresses critical gaps in existing design accessibility tools by providing comprehensive annotation capabilities specifically built for mature design systems. Unlike one-size-fits-all solutions that create noise and churn, this toolkit enables design teams to identify and prevent accessibility barriers early in the design process, improving collaboration between designers and engineers while reducing costly rework.

Expected Outcome

Organizations using the toolkit can expect to catch accessibility issues earlier in their design workflow, resulting in significant time and budget savings by preventing severe accessibility problems from reaching development. Design and engineering teams will experience improved handoff processes and deeper understanding of accessibility standards, while GitHub strengthens its position as a leader in accessibility innovation within the open-source community.
items.title: Open sourcing our Annotation Toolkit

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Single page apps (SPAs) can use GitHub authentication to sign in users, following the standards laid out in the draft RFC for Browser-Based Apps, specifically the fully browser-based architecture, as well as the refresh token handling guidelines in RFC 9700, the best current practice for OAuth 2.0 security.

SPA developers no longer need to implement an extra backend or use unsafe proxy tunnels to work around the lack of CORS support that blocked the use of SPAs. They also no longer need to include a client secret in their application in order to redeem the access token.

Expected Outcome

SPAs are a specific client type for GitHub Apps - OAuth apps do not support refresh tokens and therefore will not support SPAs. Several requirements are enforced for SPA clients, in adherence with the OAuth 2.0 standards and best practice:

  1. Clients must use the PKCE extension when requesting and redeeming the authorization code.
  2. Clients must not use a client secret when redeeming the authorization code.
  3. Refresh tokens can only be used to get a new access token for a limited time, possibly as short as 24 hours. After that clients must send the user back to GitHub to re-authenticate with the app. This re-authentication does not require entering your GitHub credentials but may require re-authenticating with your organization or enterprise SSO provider.
  4. Clients must use expiring tokens to use a SPA client. If the app has opted out of token expiration, they cannot use this pattern.
  5. CORS will be enabled on the /access_token endpoint if the authorization code was requested for a redirect URI marked as a SPA client. This allows the SPA to redeem the authorization code via XHR.
items.title: Single page app support for GitHub Apps [Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

YAML anchors are part of the standard YAML spec that GitHub Actions has not supported. Adding this support will add a reusability feature but also let Actions users take advantage of existing linters and other tools for editing and managing their YAML. It also removes a point of confusion for customers where valid YAML is not accepted by GitHub Actions by conforming to the published specification.

Expected Outcome

YAML Anchors will help customers make their Actions YAML more reusable and resolve a long-standing community issue
items.title: Support for YAML Anchors on GHEC

We want to make it easier to share and sync item information across projects. This will make it easier to keep items and their metadata up to date and remove the need for manual updates and edits.

Expected Outcome

By helping keep information up-to-date across multiple projects, teams can rely on a single source of truth where critical details remain consistent, easy to find, and free from manual effort.
items.title: Issue fields [Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

We are bringing Copilot Spaces to the IDEs: VSCode, Jetbrains, and Visual Studio.

Automate Repetitive Tasks
All software companies have routine tasks required as part of development. For example, at GitHub, we often need to add new telemetry, create new services, write test cases, or add a feature flag wrapper before we can release a new feature. These are simple tasks, but they are performed often enough to introduce toil. Sometimes, they must be done across multiple repos. Spaces can be used as a container for relevant information (such as code samples, instructions, documentation, and more), and then scaffold out the changes using Agent mode.

Review Local Changes
Many customers have specific policies related to code development such as accessibility standards, security standards, or code quality standards. Often, these are documented in a central repository as markdown. Sometimes, they are hosted on another platform like Notion or Google Drive. Spaces can be used for comparing local changes against documented standards in order to ensure compliance.

Facilitate Migrations
Library or framework upgrades can be a major challenge in some codebases. You can set up Spaces which contain documentation on the old and new frameworks, example code for both the before and after, and acceptance criteria as custom instructions.

Expected Outcome

Developers can chat with a Copilot Space or use it with agent mode in the IDE.
items.title: Copilot Spaces in the IDE

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Context is messy. Code "systems" are often abstractly defined. Documentation is often scattered, nonexistent, or outdated. This means that it can be difficult for AI agents to search and incorporate the right context autonomously.

Thankfully, in every company or codebase, someone knows where the “__” logic is defined. So as long as you can make it fast and easy for developers to set the context that they want to use and even share that with teammates, then you’ll have better quality responses.

Expected Outcome

The GA of Copilot Spaces brings the feature to all developers on github.
items.title: Copilot Spaces [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

With increasing emphasis on software supply chain security and compliance, organizations need reliable ways to ensure only trusted artifacts are promoted and released. This integration enables organizations to use GitHub-generated artifact attestations, including provenance, SBOMs, and custom attestations, as signed, verifiable evidence within JFrog’s Evidence Collection. By supporting native ingestion of GitHub attestations, customers can automatically gate the promotion of artifacts in Artifactory based on the presence and validity of attestations created by trusted GitHub workflows.

Expected Outcome

With the integration enabled, attestations generated on GitHub are automatically ingested into JFrog Evidence Collection. These attestations can then be used to enforce policies that govern artifact promotion, release readiness, and compliance requirements. For example, organizations can require that only artifacts with valid, GitHub-signed attestations are eligible for promotion or deployment, ensuring that every release meets internal and regulatory standards before reaching production.
items.title: Native integration of GitHub Artifact Attestations with JFrog Evidence for policy-driven governance
